scenes.say: Week six. Managing a brand for social purpose, with Libby Hogson from UNICEF Australia.
scenes.title: Managing a brand for social purpose
scenes.speaker: Libby Hogson

scenes.say: There are over sixty thousand Australian charities. One for every four hundred and thirty nine people. And fewer donors are giving more.

scenes.kicker: The money was in the wrong place
scenes.say: In twenty twenty UNICEF had zero unprompted awareness. Yet about ninety five percent of spend went on conversion, and five percent on awareness. The top of the funnel was empty.

note.text: Optimising a funnel whose *top was empty*.

scenes.say: Top of mind, donation intent is nineteen percent. Only prompted, it's seven. Mental availability nearly triples intent.
So the positioning: UNICEF inspires Australians with the determination it takes to protect every child, no matter what. Then say it again and again.

lines.text: UNICEF inspires Australians with the *determination* it takes to protect every child, no matter what.
Consistency is the place you hold in people’s minds, said again and again.

scenes.say: Then measure the chain. Ad awareness and share of voice drive unprompted awareness, then donation intent, then market share.
The takeaway? Brand building in a charity is brand building. Stay the course, and measure everything.

lines.text: Brand building in a charity *is* brand building.
